# Kestrel Field HSE Procedures (FICTIONAL DEMO DOCUMENT)

This is invented sample content for a software demo. The procedures below do not describe a real
operator or a real field.

## Permit to work

Hot work permits are issued by the Area Authority and expire at the end of each 12 hour shift. A new
permit is required for every shift, even when the job is unchanged. Confined space entry needs a second
person on standby at the entry point and a gas test every 30 minutes while the work is in progress.

## Emergency response

In an emergency, everyone on site goes to the muster point at the north gate and reports to the
shift supervisor for a head count. The hydrogen sulfide (H2S) alarm is set at 10 ppm. Wind socks at the
central tank battery and at the north gate show the upwind direction for evacuation.

## Spill reporting

Any spill larger than 1 barrel must be reported to the regional regulator within 24 hours. Internal
notification to the operations manager must happen within 2 hours of discovery. Smaller spills are
logged in the shift report and cleaned up before the end of the shift.

## Training and induction

All contractors must complete the Kestrel site induction before their first entry. The induction is
valid for 12 months. Employees complete an H2S awareness refresher every year, and the refresher
covers the use of escape breathing apparatus.
